GCC runtime libraries (libstdc++, libgcc, libgfortran)
GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1

The engine library is linked with -static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc, and OpenBLAS's LAPACK
routines are Fortran, so libgfortran's archive is linked in as well. Parts of those three
runtime libraries therefore end up inside the shipped library.

This is permitted, and the permission is the GCC Runtime Library Exception version 3.1:
code compiled by GCC through an Eligible Compilation Process may be combined with the
runtime libraries and distributed under the terms of the combined work, without the GPL
propagating to it. The engine is compiled by unmodified GCC with no plugins, which is an
Eligible Compilation Process.

Full text of the exception:

    https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gcc-exception-3.1.html

Full text of GPL-3.0:

    https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html

RECORDED HONESTLY: this paragraph states the licence position for the Linux library built
by this project's CI with system GCC. A library built by a different toolchain (MSVC, or a
GCC that is not stock) has a different position and this file would need revisiting.
